Clear the enemies and reach the boss!
Welcome back to reality, traveler. Or rather, what's left of it. I am Sarah, commander of the Chrono-Resistance. Take a breath — your body is adjusting to the temporal siphon.
...Where am I? The sky... it tore apart.

You are aboard the Archive Time-Ship. The people who did this to your home call themselves the Apex Archive. They are a futuristic cult siphoning the historical energy of pivotal eras to build their 'perfect' timeline. Your displacement was a side effect — but it also imbued you with Temporal Resonance, the power to fight back.
Then we must stop them. But what of the soldiers I saw? They looked like my people, but... wrong. Their eyes glowed, their weapons hummed with light.

That is the cult's doing. When the siphons deploy, the cultists use neural-linking implants to brainwash the local inhabitants of that era, forcing them to defend the siphons as 'Altered Mobs'. We must free them by destroying the siphons.
But first, we must calibrate your Temporal Resonance. Step up to the bay console.
Your combat resonance is calibrated. Now let's test your spatial awareness — you'll need every advantage to navigate the fractured timelines.
Calibration complete. The time portals are unlocked — return to the bridge and choose your first destination.
Florence... it's beautiful, but I hear the hum of machinery. These scaffoldings aren't from my books.

Stay alert. The cult has deployed a siphon in Da Vinci's workshop. The city guards have been neural-linked. They are armed with shock-pikes. Do not let their electrical discharges lock your movements.
You dare interrupt the harvest? The Archive has promised Florence eternity — and promised me your resonance.
Eternity built on stolen memories is no gift. Stand aside, or fall with your siphon.
The siphon is shattered. The energy is dispersing.
Outstanding. With the siphon gone, the neural-link is broken. The altered guards are returning to their normal states. They will wake up with nothing but a headache, thinking it was a strange dream.
I can feel it. My hands... they are glowing less. The stabilization of the area is dampening my own temporal resonance.
Yes, that is the cost. Your powers are anchored to the temporal fractures. The more we repair history, the more your resonance will fade. But it is the only way to save your world.
A small price to pay. Let's return to the ship.
The bridge is yours, traveler. The Chronal Repository will bank your dust, and the Holodeck can spar you against simulated foes.
When you are ready, the Temporal Portal is charged for your next destination. History is waiting.

To everyone who held the timeline together.
LEVEL 2: THE SIEGE OF ORLÉANS — ORLÉANS 1429
Break through the English lines toward the siege works.
The barriers are down. Take the battlement.
Orléans is starving behind those walls. And that shimmer across the causeway — no siege line in 1429 glows like that.

That is Archive hardware. Kinetic shield generators pinning the French vanguard in place, and mortar emplacements ranged on every approach. Break the generators and the cavalry charge history remembers can finally happen.
So the little ghost walks through my barriers. The Archive bought me this siege, traveler, and I intend to keep it until the walls come down.
You sold a city for borrowed lightning. Put down the lance and I might leave you your century.
The last generator is slag. The barriers are gone.
Confirmed. The vanguard is moving. The relief of Orléans is back on its own timeline, and the English commanders will remember nothing but bad weather and worse luck.
The glow in my hands dimmed again when the field collapsed. It happens every time we mend something.
It does. Your resonance is borrowed from the damage, and we are spending it repairing the damage. That arithmetic does not change, however many times you ask me.
Then let's spend it faster. Take me back to the ship.
Cross the fairgrounds and reach the Electricity Building
Rotate the conductive coils to route the beam into the receiver
The Court of Honor is open — press on!
Electric light for a mile in every direction — and every wire of it humming wrong.

That is Archive work, Traveler. They have seeded siphon coils across the fairgrounds. Let the overload land and the Exposition burns with Tesla's name on it. Reroute the current before the crowds pay for it.
Do you feel it? Alternating. Accelerating. A century of progress, and I can spend all of it in one beautiful second.
Then spend it on me. Leave the fair out of it.
Siphon coils are shattered. The current is running where it should.
Readings are settling. Every lamp on the fairgrounds is still lit — and the crowd never knew.
The resonance is fading already. I can barely feel the grid now.
It always fades once the moment is anchored. That is how we know it held.
Then anchor the next one. Bring me home, Commander.
Breach the Bastille and reach the inner courtyard
Caught in the beam! The dampener is draining your Ultimate — break the light
Blow the cell locks and free the prisoners ({0}/{1})
The prisoners have hauled the gate open — breach the inner courtyard
INNER COURTYARD BARRED — FREE THE PRISONERS
The Bastille. The crowd is at the gates — and something inside is answering them with searchlights.
Those are neural-dampening projectors, not lamps. Stay out of the beams: every second in the light bleeds off your Ultimate Meter. The cult wants this uprising too tired to finish what it started.
Citizen! You are charged with sedition against the Archive. The verdict is recorded, the sentence is eternal — and the mob will carry it out for me.
You did not come here to free anyone. You came to keep them shouting so nobody notices the siphon. Court adjourned.
The siphon is shattered. The projectors are dark.
Confirmed. The dampening field is collapsing and the prisoners are already through the inner gate. Paris takes the Bastille tonight — on its own terms, the way it was written.
The glow in my hands dimmed again. Every fracture I close takes a little more of it.
It does. Your resonance is borrowed from the damage, and we are giving the damage back. I will not pretend that is a fair trade.
It is the only trade on offer. Bring me home, Commander.
Climb sternward before the flooding overtakes you
Reach the boat deck — the water is still rising
The harvest is broken. Return to the Time-Ship.
The deck is already tilting. This ship has hours. Maybe less.

The Archive is not siphoning a battle this time, Traveler. They are draining grief — fifteen hundred lives' worth, harvested at the exact moment history remembers it happening. Get sternward before the bow goes under.
Then we take their siphon before the sea takes the ship.
Traveler, the flooding is running ahead of the historical record. Something down there is pulling water in faster than the hull can take it.
It is not the sea doing this. It is them.
Their harvester is anchored at the stern rail. Engage it and that deck will not stay dry. Keep to the gantries and finish it fast.
Sixteen hundred endings, all in one hour. Do you understand how rare a yield like this is? Stand still. You are spoiling it.
This is not a harvest. It is a grave. And you are standing in it.
The siphon is down. The water is still rising.
It has to. The sinking is real history and history stands. What we stopped was the theft — those people will be remembered instead of drained. The lifeboats are launching on schedule now.
There is something left in the wreck of the harvester. Encrypted. It keeps repeating one string.

Route it to me. Traveler, that is an uplink handshake. The Archive was never storing this haul aboard — it was relaying it upward, to an orbital communications relay that will not exist for another fifty-seven years.
Then that is where the rest of the timeline is going. Get me back to the ship, Sarah. We follow it up.
Cross the death strip unseen and reach the radar yard
In the light! A drone strike lands in seconds — break line of sight
Cut the surveillance feed relays to darken the searchlights ({0}/{1})
Every beam is dark and the radar gate is open — reach the bunker street
RADAR GATE SEALED — CUT THE SURVEILLANCE FEEDS
They are still pouring the Wall and there are already searchlights on it. Those towers are not 1961.

They are cloaked radar masts, Traveler, and the beams under them are targeting paint. Stand in one longer than a second and a half and something above the cloud deck fires straight down the column. Keep to the dark, and cut the feed relays where you find them — a mast with no feed is a mast with no beam.
Far enough. Behind me is a switchboard that speaks to every silo on this continent, and tonight it tells them a lie they have been waiting fifteen years to believe. You will not reach it.
You cut a wall through the middle of a living city and called it order. I am going to come through you the same way they will come through it.
The switchboard is dead. The masts are dark all the way to the horizon.
Confirmed. The launch order never went out. Berlin gets to survive its own division the hard, slow, human way — which is the way it was written.
It is going faint again. The resonance. Every fracture we close, I hold a little less of it.
I know. You are giving it back to the moments it was stolen from, and there is nothing aboard this ship that can pay you for that.
Then stop trying to and get me to the next one. Bring me home, Commander.
Wade the shifting dunes and find a way beneath the siege line
Find the hieroglyph seal — the order is carved somewhere in the tombs
Press the glyphs in the carved order ({0}/{1})
The vault is open — reach Cleopatra's chambers before the legion does
HIEROGLYPH SEAL — PRESS THE GLYPHS IN THE CARVED ORDER
CARVED ORDER — SCARAB · IBIS · FALCON · JACKAL
Roman siege towers on the shore — and every legionnaire down there is carrying a blade that burns.

Plasma swords and powered centurion plate, Traveler. The Archive is buying Octavian a total victory and siphoning the fall of Alexandria while it burns. The palace guard is on the same neural link. Get under the sand line: the tomb network runs beneath the siege and comes up inside the royal vault.
Then I go through the dead to reach the living.
The queen's vault opens only for those who know the old order, little ghost. I wrote the order. I wrote her ending. Kneel and be catalogued.
You put a leash on her own guard and called it worship. Step away from the door.
My royal guards... they fought with Roman steel and future fire. They turned their spears on their own queen.
The cult's mind control leaves no room for loyalty, Majesty. But look — the siphons have dissolved. The Roman legionnaires and your guards are breathing normally again. The spell is broken.
They are safe. That is what matters. Yet... the power I held. The sand obeyed my command. I could feel the flow of years in my grasp. Now, it is just dust again.
Our resonance is a symptom of a sick timeline. As the wound heals, the strength fades. We must see this through to the end.
The siphon is shattered. The sand is just sand again.
Confirmed. The neural link is down across the whole delta. Octavian's legion and the palace guard both come back to themselves, and the siege ends the way history wrote it — not one hour worse.
The queen felt her resonance go out. I felt mine dim with it.
You will feel that at every anchor we mend from here. Act II runs harder than Act I, Traveler, and the fractures ahead are bigger than one palace.
Then stop warning me and take me home, Commander. There is another one waiting.
Get the citizens out before Vesuvius buries the city
Balance the winch — both stone pans must carry the same load
The road east is open. Run.
The flow caught you — keep moving east!
Reach the thermal anchor on the caldera rim
The harvest is broken. Return to the Time-Ship.
ROAD BURIED — HAUL THE ROCKFALL CLEAR
The mountain is already open. That ash column is miles high — and it is coming down far faster than it should be.

Faster is the whole point, Traveler. The Archive has driven thermal anchors into the caldera to tap the eruption at its peak. They are forcing Vesuvius ahead of its own schedule so the yield lands before anyone in Pompeii can reach the harbour.
Then I get them to the harbour first. The anchor second.
Eighteen hours of terror, compressed into two. Do you understand what that concentration is worth? Every one of them running, and not one of them fast enough.
They were never running from the mountain. They were running from you.
The anchor is down. The mountain sounds ordinary again — as ordinary as that ever gets.
Confirmed. Vesuvius is back on its own clock: eighteen hours, exactly the way it was written. That is enough time. The south road is moving and the harbour is answering.
It went dim again. Further than last time. Halfway up the ash road I felt it go out completely, for a second.
I saw it on the telemetry. Your resonance is drawn out of the fracture, and every fracture you close is a little less of you. I am logging it, Traveler. I will not pretend it is not happening.
Log it, and bring me home. There are nine more of these.
The Navy is shelling the harbour. Get to the moorings.
Cross the channel and board the burning flagship.
The targeting grid is dead. Return to the Time-Ship.
They voted. A whole town of thieves stood up and voted itself free — and the sky is full of mortars.

Those are not Navy guns, Traveler, not entirely. The Archive has seeded the water with sub-aquatic torpedoes and laid a chronal targeting grid over the bay. Every shell the British fire is being aimed for them. Nassau is not being defeated. It is being erased on schedule.
Then we go where the grid is anchored. Out to the ships.
Look at it burn. A republic of nobodies, and history was going to keep the name anyway. I am simply correcting the ledger.
They are not nobodies. They are the first people here who chose. Get off their harbour.
The grid is down. The guns are just guns again.
Confirmed — the bay is clear of chronal returns. Nassau still falls to the pardon in two years, Traveler, but it falls the way it actually fell, and everyone below decks gets to run for the boats.
The resonance is thinning again. I could feel every rope before I touched it, and now I can barely feel my own hands.
It always fades once the fracture closes. Come home and let the ship read you. There is another siphon burning three hundred years further back, and I do not like where.
Cross the yard and get up onto the stage
Cross the stage — the boards shake before they drop
The galleries have you marked — move!
Swing the rigging up through the galleries to the tiring-house
Full house. Two thousand people packed in to watch a prince go mad, and not one of them has blinked since I walked in.

That is the manipulators, Traveler. The Archive has seeded the galleries, and it has rigged collapse charges under the stage. The moment those boards go, two thousand held minds are released at once and they all try to leave through the same door. Keep off a plank that starts shaking — and keep moving. A held crowd throws whatever is in reach at anything that stands still.
Then I will give them a performance worth watching.
You are early, and you are not in the script. Sit down. The fifth act is the only part of any of this that anyone remembers, and I have rewritten it so that nobody walks out.
Every one of them came here to watch a tragedy and then go home again. I am going to make sure they do.
Charges are out from under the boards. The galleries let go all at once — listen to them. They are arguing about the ending.
Confirmed. Two thousand people walk out of the Globe tonight and take that argument home with them, which is exactly what was written.
It went faint again. Halfway across the rigging I reached for the resonance and there was a beat where nothing came back.
I saw it on the telemetry. Every fracture you seal, you hand a little more of it back to the moment it was stolen from. I am not going to pretend that is free.
Then log it and line up the next one. Bring me home, Commander.
Advance east across the battlefield — use the fences and sandbags for cover.
Both arrays are down. The Union line has the breastwork — follow it into the railcut.
CONFEDERATE BREASTWORK — BREAK THE SHIELDING ARRAYS
That is not cannon fire. Those shells are tracking — they turn to follow me.

Confirmed. The Archive handed the Confederate batteries laser guidance and an electromagnetic screen, and Union brigades are pinned in the open. Two shielding arrays hold that screen up. Break both and the line moves. Keep something solid between you and the sky, Traveler — those guns telegraph before they fire.
RAILHEAD SECURE. TARGET RESOLVED. THE FIELD BELONGS TO THE GUN.
Then come off the rails and say that where I can reach you.
The gun is dead. The sky is quiet. First time all day I can hear the wheat.

Siphon shattered — the whole Gettysburg draw just went dark on my board. The Union advance is over the wall and the battle is running on its own clock again. Whatever the Archive wrote here is unwritten.
Sarah. Climbing that last bank I reached for the resonance and for half a second there was nothing there. Just me.
I saw it on the telemetry. The gap is longer every level. I am not going to dress that up for you — every fracture you close is drawn out of you, and I am logging every second of it.
Log it. Then pull me out. There are four more of these.
Cross the mare and reach the Archive outpost
Mind the vacuum vents — the low route is the loud route
Ride the spire lift and take the highline over the curtain wall
The broadcast is clean. Return to the Time-Ship.
Tranquility Base is right there. The lander, the flag, the first footprints ever pressed into this dust — and half a kilometre east of it, something the crew will never see and never report.

That is the relay, Traveler. The uplink handshake we pulled out of the Titanic wreck was pointing here all along — fifty-seven years early, and this is the address. The Archive is riding the broadcast: six hundred million people watching one moment together, and every one of them feeding the siphon. Watch your footing. One sixth of the gravity you are used to, and the outpost vents run straight to vacuum.
Then we take the relay before the broadcast ends.
To think humanity would walk among the stars... and yet, the cult has built a fortress of metal here.

This is the Act II siphon nexus. If they extract this milestone, the future's memory of human space exploration will be completely erased. We are going to trigger the final overload process. But be warned: once the prime anchor at Alexandria is restored in the final act, the timeline will snap back to normal.
And what happens to us then?

Every brainwashed local across all eras will be restored to their true self — safe, home, and entirely unaware of this nightmare. You will return to your own time as well. You will carry the memory of this voyage... but you will lose all of your powers, since the changes were centred on your displacement. You will be mortal again.
Then let us make this final legacy count.

Six hundred million witnesses, one signal, one instant. Do you know what a species remembers hardest? The first time it left. I will take that from them, and they will never learn the shape of the hole where it was.
They came up here on arithmetic and nerve, and they came up here together. You do not get to hold that.
The relay is scrap. The broadcast is going out clean.

Confirmed. Every set on Earth is watching the real thing. The outpost crew the Archive pressed into service are already coming back to themselves — nobody down there will remember having been anything but themselves.
It went out completely on the pad, Sarah. The resonance. For a second I was just a person standing on the Moon. Whatever we do next, I should do it soon.

I know, and I have the reason we can. The overload wrote something back down the beam before it died — a coordinate signature. Traveler, it is not anywhere in history. It is their home. Far future. Neo-Earth.
Then Act Two ends here. Take me through their front door, Commander.
Cross the rift and find the far corridor
Ride the loose era fragments — the shelf below is pooled with stalled time
The corridor is open. Return to the Time-Ship.

There is no ground here. There is no here here — only pieces. That is the flag from Tranquility Base, and that is a Bastille door, and they are falling past each other without either of them falling down.

You are between dimensions, Traveler. The trace we pulled off the Overseer runs straight through it — the Archive cut a corridor from their own century back through every fracture they ever made, and this is the spoil heap. Head east. The far side opens on Neo-Earth.
Then I walk east on Orléans stone and Titanic decking. Tell me the moment the gravity is about to turn over.

You have shed a piece of yourself in every century you closed. Did you think they went nowhere? I am every second of resonance the fractures took out of you, and I still remember the shape it left behind.
Then you know exactly how I fight, and exactly how tired I am. So do I. Come on.
It went down the way I would have gone down. Same guard, same tell, same half-second too late. I have never had to watch myself lose before.

The corridor is holding. There was no siphon in here to shatter — the rift stopped tearing the moment that thing stopped drawing on it. And nothing living was ever caught in the Void, so there is nobody down there to send home. For once I have no casualty list to read you.
Sarah, when it went out I reached for the resonance and for a second I could not tell whose it was. I could not tell which one of us was still standing.

I know. It is on my board and I am not going to dress it up. That was the price, and it is closer now than it was on the Moon. But the far end of this corridor is their front door, and it is standing open.
Then let it be me who walks through it. Take me to Neo-Earth, Commander.
Time the perimeter lattice and breach the outer wall
Ride the containment pockets over the sealed bulkhead
Run the fabrication spine to the security core
The core is dark. Only Alexandria is left.
There is no sky here. Just the machine — all the way up, all the way down — and not one person in it who was ever taken. Everything in this place is here because it chose to be.

That is Neo-Earth, Traveler. Not a stolen era: their own. The Apex Archive's core laboratory, the room every siphon in history reported back to. It was built to keep people out, so the perimeter will be honest about it — security lattices on a fixed cycle, and anti-gravity containment fields they use to shift cargo. Read a lattice before you walk it. And mind the pockets: they will lift you a great deal further than you expect.
Then let us walk into the one place they never rehearsed losing.
You are a rounding error that learned to knock. I have catalogued every version of this conversation, and in the ones that matter you were filed a long time ago.
